gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Synology rates the DS425+ for at most 10 SMB connections (FSCT-based), exactly a 10-person office with no headroom. The DS925+, DS925neo+ and DS1525+ are each rated for 40, and the DS425+ also has no expansion-unit port, while the DS925+ takes one DX525 for 9 bays.
standout_why: I read our page, computingforgeeks.com/best-nas-for-small-business (cited), starryhope.com/nas/best-4-bay-nas (top result), synology.com/en-us/products/DS925+ (cited) and qnap.com TS-464 hardware specs (cited). Computingforgeeks and Starry Hope already cover the DSM 7.3 third-party-drive reversal and the rule that M.2 pools need Synology-listed SSDs, so the drive policy would not stand out. Starry Hope names the DS425+ only for its 2019 J4125 CPU and 2 GB RAM. Its SMB connection limit, DX525 expansion support and memory ceiling were stated on none of these pages. The cited DS925+ product page does list its own figure of 40, but nothing in ChatGPT's results gives the DS425+ figure or puts the two side by side. That matters because ChatGPT's latest run (2026-11-13 19:58) suggested the DS425+ as a lower-cost Synology for this 10-person office. Our own page lists the DS425+ and gives no connection limit. No page names TS-464 10GbE card models or the DS925neo+ rule against mixing ECC and non-ECC memory.
decides: This rules the DS425+ out as the office pick. Its maker rating is 10 SMB connections, the whole headcount with no growth room. It also stops at 6 GB RAM and takes no expansion unit. That confirms the DS925+ as the Synology pick, rated for 40 connections, with 32 GB RAM and +5 bays via the DX525. The DS925neo+, launched in the US on 2026-10-21, is the cheaper way to keep that rating, but it ships with non-ECC memory and Synology does not support mixing it with ECC modules. If the office later needs 10GbE, the TS-464 takes QNAP-listed cards such as the QXG-10G1T in its PCIe Gen3 x2 slot. The DS925+ and DS925neo+ have no slot at all.

findings.label: Maximum SMB connections (FSCT-based)
findings.note: Synology footnote: tested fully populated with Synology SATA HDDs and all onboard ports, Microsoft FSCT 1.3, HomeFolder workload, 600 s, Windows Server 2022 domain controller, 8 Windows 10 clients, directory leasing enabled. Also on the DS425+ product spec page (https://www.synology.com/en-us/products/DS425+#specs, read 2026-11-13).

findings.label: Maximum SMB connections (FSCT-based)
findings.note: Same FSCT test as the DS425+. That is 4× the DS425+ rating and 4× a 10-person office.

findings.label: Maximum SMB connections (FSCT-based)
findings.note: The DS1525+ is also rated 40 on the same page.

findings.label: Expansion unit and memory ceiling
findings.value: No expansion port or expansion unit listed; 2 GB non-ECC + one D4NS01-4G = 6 GB maximum
findings.note: The page also notes that the 1GbE port's MTU is limited to 1500 (no jumbo frames on that port). The DS425+ has 1× 1GbE + 1× 2.5GbE.

findings.label: Expansion unit pairing
findings.value: 1× DX525 over the USB Type-C expansion port; 9 drive bays maximum
findings.note: The DS925neo+ also takes 1× DX525 (9 bays). The DS1525+ takes up to 2× DX525 (15 bays), per https://www.synology.com/en-us/products/compare/DS1525%2B/DS925neo%2B.

findings.label: Compatible memory modules
findings.value: D4ES04-4G, D4ES03-8G, D4ES03-16G; 32 GB maximum (16 GB × 2); modules must be identical, same model number
findings.note: Synology states that with non-Synology memory it will not provide full product warranty or technical support. Ships with 4 GB DDR4 ECC.

findings.label: Memory pairing exclusion
findings.value: Ships with 4 GB non-ECC DDR4; supports Synology ECC upgrades to 32 GB, but mixing non-ECC and ECC modules is not officially supported
findings.source_title: Press Releases | Synology Inc. (DiskStation neo+ Series)
findings.note: US press release dated 2026-10-21, availability at Amazon, B&H and Canada Computers. Per this release, the PCIe 3.0 slot for 10/25GbE is only on the DS1525neo+ and DS1825neo+, not the DS925neo+.

findings.label: Third-party drive pairing (DSM 7.3)
findings.value: 25-model-year Plus/Value/J units on DSM 7.3 can install and build storage pools on non-validated third-party drives; M.2 storage pools and M.2 cache still require drives on Synology's HCL
findings.note: Release dated 2025-10-08. Applies to the DS925+, DS425+ and DS1525+. The product page still says Synology 'only guarantees full functionality, reliability, and performance for compatible drives'. Computingforgeeks and Starry Hope already carry this.

findings.label: 10GbE upgrade pairing
findings.value: E10G22-T1-Mini in 1× PCIe Gen3 x2 network upgrade slot
findings.note: No PCIe slot or 10GbE card is listed for the DS925+ (product page) or the DS925neo+ (same compare page).

findings.label: 10GbE / network card pairing
findings.value: 1× PCIe Gen3 x2 slot (max card 190 × 68.9 × 18.76 mm); listed cards: QXG-10G1T, QXG-10G2SF-NXE, QXG-10G2T, QXG-10G2TB (EOL), QXG-25G2SF-CX6, QXG-2G1T-I225, QXG-2G2T-I225, QXG-2G4T-I225, QXG-5G1T-111C, QXG-5G2T-111C (EOL)
findings.note: Per the same page, bundled accessories such as expansion cards and the power adapter carry a 1-year warranty versus 3 years for the unit.

findings.label: Memory and M.2 limits
findings.value: 8 GB installed, 16 GB maximum (2 × 8 GB); 2× M.2 2280 at PCIe Gen3 x1, not hot-swappable
findings.note: QNAP: 'Use only QNAP memory modules to maintain system performance and stability'. It warns that unsupported modules can stop the OS from booting.
